description: Table 1 is a single-panel composition table (a table rendered as an image; no sub-panels) giving the chemical composition of two experimental Fe–Mn–Al–C low-density steels. It is a 9-column × 2-row grid whose column headers are the elements Fe, Mn, Al, C, Si, Cr, Mo, V and Ti, and whose row headers are the steel designations M1 and M2. Fe is reported as "Bal." (balance) for both steels. Row M1: Mn 20.17, Al 8.12, C 0.61, Si 0.17, Cr 0.40, Mo 0.31, with V and Ti both shown as "–" (no entry). Row M2: Mn 20.04, Al 8.05, C 0.85, Si 0.18, Cr 0.42, Mo 0.34, V 0.62 and Ti 0.09. No unit row or unit label is printed on the table image itself; the caption states only "Chemical composition of experimental steels". The table's role is to establish that M2 differs from M1 mainly by a higher carbon level (0.61 → 0.85) together with the additions of 0.62 V and 0.09 Ti, i.e. the base composition for the Ti/V-modified variant of the low-density steel.

subfigures.description: Single composition table (9 element columns: Fe, Mn, Al, C, Si, Cr, Mo, V, Ti) with two rows for the experimental steels M1 and M2. Fe = Bal. for both; M1 has V and Ti marked '–', M2 has V 0.62 and Ti 0.09. No unit label printed on the table image.

observations.observation: The table contains exactly two steel rows, labelled M1 and M2, and nine element columns: Fe, Mn, Al, C, Si, Cr, Mo, V, Ti.
For both M1 and M2 the Fe column reads 'Bal.', i.e. iron is the balance of the composition.
M1 composition as printed: Mn 20.17, Al 8.12, C 0.61, Si 0.17, Cr 0.40, Mo 0.31, and '–' for both V and Ti.
M2 composition as printed: Mn 20.04, Al 8.05, C 0.85, Si 0.18, Cr 0.42, Mo 0.34, V 0.62, Ti 0.09.
The table image prints no unit row or unit label (e.g. wt.%) for the element values, so the concentration basis is not stated in the figure itself.
M2 has a higher carbon content than M1 (0.85 vs 0.61) and is the only steel containing V (0.62) and Ti (0.09); Mn, Al, Si, Cr and Mo are nearly the same in the two steels.
The caption identifies the table as the 'Chemical composition of experimental steels'.
The citing text states that the difference in carbon content of the two components is mainly because of the combination of Ti and V.

The citing text states the materials were melted in a high-vacuum electric-arc melting furnace, hot rolled from 20 to 2 mm at 1000 °C, water quenched, solution-processed at 1000 °C for 30 min and water quenched, then aged at 550 °C for 10 h and 30 h with water quenching.
The citing text names the solution-treated steels M1-SS and M2-SS and the aged steels M1-30, M2-10 and M2-30.
The citing text states the paper concerns a low-density steel with strong carbide-forming elements Ti and V used to regulate carbon distribution and control κ-carbide precipitation.
